docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Variable Monitoring module collects, aggregates, and analyzes input and output variables from every rule engine execution, helping operators detect data quality issues and abnormal rule behavior.

Data pipeline: Rule Execution → ClickHouse raw logs → 5-minute materialized view pre-aggregation → Daily scheduled aggregation into MySQL at 02:00 AM.

docs.title: Storage Architecture
docs.text: Tier Storage Description Raw Layer ClickHouse execution_var_log One row per variable per execution, 3-month TTL Pre-aggregation Layer ClickHouse execution_var_log_5m Materialized view with automatic 5-minute window aggregation Daily Stats Layer MySQL ruleuler_variable_daily_stats Aggregated daily at 02:00 AM via scheduled job

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• monitoring.enabled=true in application.yml
  • ClickHouse deployed and initialized (deploy/clickhouse/init.sql)
  • User granted the menu:monitoring permission

docs.title: 1. Real-Time Overview
docs.text:
Path: Monitoring → Select Project and Knowledge Package

Displays today vs. yesterday summary metrics:

  • Total executions
  • Anomaly rate (missing value ratio)
  • Error rate (failed execution ratio)

Data source: ClickHouse materialized view execution_var_log_5m, grouped by today() / yesterday().

docs.title: 2. Variable List
docs.text:
Displays real-time metrics for all active variables today:

Metric Description sample_count Number of samples missing_rate Missing value ratio error_rate Execution error ratio mean Mean value (numeric variables) min / max Minimum / Maximum values alert_flags Active alert flags

Supported sort orders: Anomaly first (default), Missing rate, Error rate, Sample count.

Alert flags are computed by AlertChecker against configured thresholds: - Missing rate exceeds missing_rate_max - Outlier rate exceeds outlier_rate_max - Absolute skewness exceeds skewness_abs_max

docs.title: 3. DoD / WoW Comparison
docs.text:
Enhanced variable list mode showing Day-over-Day (vs. yesterday) and Week-over-Week (vs. 7 days ago) percentage changes:

  • dod_mean_pct: Day-over-Day mean change
  • dod_missing_rate_pct: Day-over-Day missing rate change
  • wow_mean_pct: Week-over-Week mean change
  • wow_missing_rate_pct: Week-over-Week missing rate change

Baseline source: MySQL ruleuler_variable_daily_stats records from 1 day and 7 days ago.

docs.title: 4. Variable Trend
docs.text:
Path: Variable List → Click Variable Name

Displays daily statistical trends for a single variable over a selected date range (default 30 days, up to 3 months):

  • Mean, standard deviation, quantiles (P25 / P50 / P75)
  • Missing rate, outlier rate
  • Skewness

Data source: MySQL ruleuler_variable_daily_stats.

docs.title: 5. Intraday Missing Rate Spike Detection
docs.text: Displays 5-minute granularity missing rate trends for today, flagging sudden spikes when a window's missing rate increases by more than missing_rate_spike_delta over the previous window.

docs.title: 6. PSI Distribution Stability
docs.text:
PSI (Population Stability Index) measures distribution drift for numeric variables:

  • Baseline distribution: Raw val_num over the past 30 days in ClickHouse
  • Current distribution: Today's raw val_num
  • Computed across 10 equal-frequency bins
PSI Value Interpretation < 0.1 Stable distribution 0.1 ~ 0.2 Moderate drift (warning) > 0.2 Significant drift (alert)

Thresholds are configurable via psi_warning and psi_alert. Calculated for numeric variables only.

docs.title: 7. Enum Drift Detection
docs.text:
For categorical variables (String / Boolean), detects changes in the top value or its frequency share:

  • Baseline: 7-day average of top_value and top_freq_ratio from MySQL ruleuler_variable_daily_stats
  • Current: Today's raw distribution from ClickHouse
  • Drift triggered when top_value changes or frequency share shifts by more than enum_drift_threshold

docs.title: 8. Period Comparison
docs.text: Compare statistical metrics of selected variables across two custom time ranges (up to 3 months per period), aggregated in real time from ClickHouse.

docs.title: 9. Version Comparison
docs.text:
Compare variable metrics before and after a knowledge package release based on publish timestamps in ruleuler_rule_file_version:

  • Period A: Release A → Release B
  • Period B: Release B → Present
  • Dimensions: Sample count, missing rate, error rate, mean

docs.title: 10. Execution Logs & Execution Trace
docs.text:
Paginated query of historical executions grouped by execution_id:

  • Execution timestamp, duration, variable count, status (success / failed)
  • Click an execution to inspect all input/output variable values

Execution Trace: In the execution detail view, the system displays the full execution trace path stored in ClickHouse execution_trace_log: - Matched rule nodes and evaluated conditions - Real-time variable assignments (VarAssign) and per-node execution time

docs.title: 11. Anomaly Drill-Down
docs.text: Click an alert tag in the variable list to inspect specific anomalous execution records filtered by missing, error, or outlier.

docs.title: 12. Intraday Volume Trend
docs.text: 5-minute granularity comparison of today vs. yesterday execution volume, missing count, error count, anomaly rate, and error rate.

docs.title: 13. Last N Days Trend
docs.text: Daily execution trend over the past N days (default 14 days), including total executions, error executions, missing executions, error rate, and anomaly rate.

docs.title: Alert Configuration
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET/PUT /api/monitoring/alert-config

Parameter Default Description missing_rate_max 0.05 Missing rate alert threshold missing_rate_spike_delta 0.1 Intraday missing rate spike threshold outlier_rate_max 0.03 Outlier rate alert threshold skewness_abs_max 2.0 Absolute skewness alert threshold psi_warning 0.1 PSI warning threshold psi_alert 0.2 PSI alert threshold enum_drift_threshold 0.15 Categorical frequency drift threshold

Stored in the single-row MySQL table ruleuler_monitoring_alert_config with a 5-minute in-memory cache.

docs.title: Manual Aggregation
docs.text:
Daily stats are aggregated automatically at 02:00 AM. To trigger aggregation manually:

# Aggregate yesterday's stats
curl -X POST http://localhost:16009/api/monitoring/aggregate

# Aggregate a specific date
curl -X POST http://localhost:16009/api/monitoring/aggregate?date=2026-04-05

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
RulEuler uses Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to enforce two-tier authorization across frontend menus and backend REST APIs.

Model relationship: User → Role → Permission (many-to-many).

docs.title: User (rbac_user)
docs.text:
Field Description username Unique login username password_hash BCrypt password hash status 1 = Enabled, 0 = Disabled built_in 1 = Built-in user (cannot be deleted)

Default built-in user: admin / asdfg@1234.

docs.title: Role (rbac_role)
docs.text:
Field Description name Unique role name description Role description built_in 1 = Built-in role (cannot be deleted)

Default built-in role: admin (super administrator with all permissions).

docs.title: Permission (rbac_permission)
docs.text: Field Description permission_code Unique permission identifier name Display name type menu (frontend menu visibility) or api (backend operation access) parent_id Parent permission ID for hierarchical grouping

docs.title: Menu Permissions
docs.text:
Format: menu:{module}, controlling frontend navigation visibility.

Permission Code Description menu:dashboard Dashboard menu:projects Project Management menu:console Rule Editor menu:system System Settings menu:system:users User Management menu:system:roles Role Management menu:system:audit Audit Logs menu:monitoring Variable Monitoring menu:approvals Release Approvals

docs.title: API & Action Permissions
docs.text: Permission Code Description api:GET:/api/rbac/users View user list api:POST:/api/rbac/users Create user api:PUT:/api/rbac/users Edit user api:DELETE:/api/rbac/users Delete user api:PUT:/api/rbac/users/roles Assign user roles api:GET:/api/rbac/roles View role list api:POST:/api/rbac/roles Create role api:PUT:/api/rbac/roles Edit role api:DELETE:/api/rbac/roles Delete role api:PUT:/api/rbac/roles/permissions Assign role permissions api:GET:/api/rbac/roles/permissions View permission list api:GET:/api/monitoring/* Query monitoring data pack:publish:submit Submit & publish release requests pack:publish:approve Approve or reject release requests project:function:upload Upload custom function JARs project:function:view View custom functions

docs.title: 1. JWT Authentication (JwtAuthFilter)
docs.text:
All /api/** requests require a valid JWT token via:

  • Header: Authorization: Bearer {token}
  • Or Cookie: ruleuler_token={token}

Whitelisted public paths: /api/auth/login, /api/auth/register, and static assets.

docs.title: 2. RBAC Filter (RbacPermissionFilter)
docs.text:
Intercepts /api/rbac/** requests:

  1. Users with the admin role or * wildcard permission are granted access immediately
  2. Normalizes numeric ID segments (/api/rbac/users/123 → /api/rbac/users) and matches api:{METHOD}:{normalizedPath} against the user's permission set

docs.title: 3. Annotation Guard (@RequirePermission)
docs.text:
Protects non-/api/rbac/ endpoints via AOP:

@RequirePermission("pack:publish:submit")
public ApiResult submit(...) { ... }

docs.title: 4. Frontend Menu Control
docs.text:
The frontend checks permissions via the usePermission hook:

const canMonitoring = usePermission('menu:monitoring');
const canApproval = usePermission('menu:approvals');

docs.title: API
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/rbac/users List users (filter by keyword/roleId) POST /api/rbac/users Create user PUT /api/rbac/users/{id} Update user DELETE /api/rbac/users/{id} Delete user PUT /api/rbac/users/{id}/roles Assign roles to user GET /api/rbac/roles List roles POST /api/rbac/roles Create role PUT /api/rbac/roles/{id} Update role DELETE /api/rbac/roles/{id} Delete role PUT /api/rbac/roles/{id}/permissions Assign permissions to role GET /api/rbac/roles/permissions List all permissions

docs.title: REA Expression Syntax
docs.text:
REA (Rule Expression Assistant) is RulEuler's text-based rule editor that compiles human-readable expressions into executable rule XML.

System keywords and operators are all uppercase. Variable names, parameter names, and string literals preserve their exact case as defined in libraries.

docs.title: Expression Structure
docs.text:
Each rule consists of three clauses:

Clause Meaning Syntax When (如果) Condition variable OPERATOR value [AND/OR ...], supports value functions Then (那么) Matched actions variable = value or action functions, separated by ; Else (否则) Unmatched actions Same as Then

docs.title: Reference Format
docs.text:
Type Format Example Variable Category.fieldName FlightInfo.arrival_time Parameter Bare parameter name can_score

Property names may coincide with reserved words (FlightInfo.WEEK and Order.MONTH are valid). Category names and parameter names cannot use reserved namespace identifiers (WEEK.foo or bare DATE is invalid).

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Applicable Types == Equal to All != Not equal to All > >= < <= Numeric / date comparison Number, Date CONTAIN / NOTCONTAIN Contains / does not contain substring String IN / NOTIN In / not in list All MATCH / NOTMATCH Regex match / non-match String STARTWITH / ENDWITH Prefix / suffix match String EQUALSIGNORECASE Case-insensitive equality String

Operators must be uppercase. Contain, In, or and will fail validation.

docs.title: Value Types
docs.text: Type Syntax Example String Double-quoted "International" Number Numeric literal 5, -3.14 Boolean TRUE / FALSE TRUE Variable reference Category.fieldName FlightInfo.gate_id Parameter reference Bare parameter name threshold List Comma-separated in parentheses ("A", "B", "C") Function call See below TRIM(FlightInfo.name) Arithmetic + - * / % with spaces around operators FlightInfo.score + 10

docs.title: Boolean Type
docs.text:
Boolean variables and boolean-returning functions support both implicit and explicit forms:

In conditions:

# Implicit — equivalent to == TRUE
FlightInfo.is_international
LISTEMPTY(FlightInfo.tags)

# Explicit
FlightInfo.is_international == TRUE
FlightInfo.is_international == FALSE

In assignments:

FlightInfo.is_international = TRUE

Warning

Boolean literals must be uppercase TRUE / FALSE. true or True will report a syntax error.

docs.title: Null Checks: ISNULL / ISNOTNULL
docs.text:
Null predicates in conditions (aligned with LISTEMPTY). They compile to the engine's native null / not-null assertors rather than functions, so they cannot be assigned or compared with ==.

ISNULL(FlightInfo.gate)
ISNOTNULL(FlightInfo.gate)
ISNULL(FlightInfo.gate) AND FlightInfo.score > 0
ISNULL(TRIM(FlightInfo.name))
ISNULL(FlightInfo.score) OR FlightInfo.score == -999

Invalid forms: FlightInfo.gate NULL (no postfix syntax), ISNULL(x) == TRUE, flag = ISNULL(x), ISNULL(1), ISNULL(score + 10).

For sentinel default values (e.g., -999 representing missing data), use == -999.

Empty String Behavior in ISNULL Between Engine and Gray Evaluator

For ISNULL(""): the core engine's NullAssertor treats blank strings as null (isBlank → true), whereas the gray release ConditionEvaluator checks strict == null (false). Missing fields and null evaluate to true in both paths.

docs.title: Gray Release SDK Compatibility
docs.text: condition_expr is evaluated locally on ruleuler-client. Legacy postfix x NULL / x Null remains supported in the gray evaluator, while new ISNULL(...) or arithmetic expressions require an up-to-date ruleuler-client.

docs.title: Arithmetic: + - * / %
docs.text:
On the left side of a comparison, only "one atom + numeric constants" is allowed: FlightInfo.score + 10 > 80. Adding two variables on the left side is not allowed — assign to a parameter first or place the expression on the right side. Numeric literals cannot appear on the left side of a comparison.

Full arithmetic expressions are supported on the right side of assignments, the right side of comparisons, and inside function arguments:

can_score = FlightInfo.score + 10
can_score = FlightInfo.amount * 1.1
can_score = ABS(FlightInfo.score) + 10
can_score = 1.1 * (FlightInfo.score + 10)
ABS(FlightInfo.score + 10) > 5

Operator precedence: * / % bind tighter than + - (MVEL rules). Parentheses may only appear on the right side of an arithmetic operator: write 1.1 * (score + 10) instead of (score + 10) * 1.1.

Binary arithmetic operators require spaces on both sides: score - 10 is valid; score-10 and score -10 are invalid.

Comparing two compound arithmetic expressions (score + a > bonus + b) is invalid — assign one side to a parameter first.

No Numeric Literal on the Left of a Comparison

80 < score + bonus is invalid in both full and gray execution because the engine's left-hand slot does not accept literals. Use a variable or parameter on the left side.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
REA exposes a unified function call syntax that compiles down to native engine Method / CommonFunction nodes without altering runtime execution.

Value functions can be used on either side of a condition or on the right side of an assignment. Action functions (void) can only be used as statements in Then / Else blocks (LISTSORT works in both contexts).

# Flat call (recommended)
TRIM(FlightInfo.name) == ""
LISTEMPTY(FlightInfo.tags) AND MAPHAS(FlightInfo.extra, "k")
ABS(FlightInfo.score) >= 10
NOW()

# Namespaced call (for autocomplete grouping / disambiguation)
STRING.TRIM(FlightInfo.name)
MATH.ABS(FlightInfo.score)
DATE.NOW()
LIST.SIZE(FlightInfo.tags)

# Collection aggregation (second argument is a bare property name)
COUNT(Order.items) > 0
SUM(Order.items, amount) > 1000

# Assignments
gate_type = TRIM(FlightInfo.gate_id)
can_score = ABS(MIN(FlightInfo.score, 100))

# Then / Else action functions (void return)
LISTADD(FlightInfo.tags, "INTL"); risk_level = "high"
MAPPUT(FlightInfo.extra, "level", "VIP")

Invalid examples:

LISTADD(FlightInfo.tags, "VIP") == TRUE      # Action functions cannot be used in conditions
can_score = LISTADD(FlightInfo.tags, "VIP")  # Action functions do not return a value
TRIM(FlightInfo.name)                        # Value functions must be assigned, not standalone statements
listAdd(xs, "VIP")                           # Function names must be uppercase
SUM(Order.items.amount)                      # Second argument is a bare property name, not a dotted path

Namespace prefixes STRING, MATH, DATE, LIST, and MAP are reserved (case-insensitive) and cannot be used as category or parameter names.

docs.title: String Functions → urule.stringAction
docs.text: TRIM SUBSTRING SUBSTRINGFROM SUBSTRINGTO LOWER UPPER LENGTH CHARAT INDEXOF LASTINDEXOF REPLACE SPLIT

docs.title: Math Functions → urule.mathAction
docs.text: ABS MAX MIN (two scalars, not collections) SIN COS TAN COT LN LOG10 ROUND

docs.title: Date Functions → urule.dateAction
docs.text:
NOW PARSEDATE FORMATDATE ADDYEARS / ADDMONTHS / ADDDAYS / ADDHOURS / ADDMINUTES / ADDSECONDS and corresponding SUB*. YEAR MONTH WEEK DAY HOUR MINUTE SECOND. DIFFMILLIS / DIFFSECONDS / DIFFMINUTES / DIFFHOURS / DIFFDAYS / DIFFWEEKS / DIFFMONTHS.

Engine Date Quirks

  • MONTH returns 0–11 (0 = January, so MONTH(NOW()) == 9 is October)
  • WEEK returns Calendar.DAY_OF_WEEK: 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday
  • DAY maps to the engine's getay method

docs.title: List / Map Functions
docs.text:
Value functions: LISTSIZE LISTMAX LISTMIN LISTCONTAINS LISTEMPTY LISTSORT LISTRETRIVE MAPGET MAPSIZE MAPHAS

Action functions (Then / Else only): LISTADD LISTREMOVE MAPPUT MAPREMOVE

For LISTSORT / LISTRETRIVE, pass the property name as a bare identifier or string literal: LISTSORT(Order.items, amount, "正序"). Note that ascending sort in the core engine only recognizes "1", "true", or "正序"; any other string (including "asc") sorts in descending order.

docs.title: Collection Aggregation → CommonFunction
docs.text: COUNT(xs) takes a collection. SUM, AVG, MAXOF, and MINOF take a collection and a bare property name: SUM(Order.items, amount).

docs.title: Custom Functions (Project Action Library)
docs.text:
Spring Bean methods registered in an action library (.al.xml) use the same BEAN.METHOD(...) uppercase syntax in REA (matched case-insensitively against the action library):

RISKSERVICE.SCORE(FlightInfo.airline, 10)

For packaging and uploading custom function JARs, see Custom Functions.

docs.title: Condition Expression Examples
docs.text:
FlightInfo.arrival_time > 5
FlightInfo.arrival_time > 5 AND FlightInfo.is_international
FlightInfo.airline IN ("CA", "MU", "CZ")
FlightInfo.arrival_time > 5 AND (FlightInfo.flight_type == "Domestic" OR FlightInfo.flight_type == "International")
ABS(FlightInfo.score) >= 10 AND LISTCONTAINS(FlightInfo.tags, "VIP")
ISNULL(FlightInfo.gate) OR FlightInfo.score + 10 > 80
threshold < FlightInfo.score + FlightInfo.bonus

Note

Mixing AND and OR at the same nesting level is not allowed; use parentheses to group them explicitly.

docs.title: Action Expression Examples
docs.text:
can_score = 5
can_score = 5; risk_level = "high"
can_score = ABS(FlightInfo.score)
can_score = FlightInfo.amount * 1.1
can_score = 1.1 * (FlightInfo.score + 10)
LISTADD(FlightInfo.tags, "INTL"); risk_level = "high"

docs.title: Autocomplete
docs.text:
• Without .: suggests variable categories, parameters, operators, AND/OR, TRUE/FALSE, ISNULL(), and functions
  • After .: suggests fields within the selected variable category
  • After STRING. / MATH. / DATE. / LIST. / MAP. or custom Bean prefixes: suggests methods in that namespace
  • Selecting a function inserts FUNC() with the cursor placed inside the parentheses
  • Action functions such as LISTADD are filtered out in condition clauses

docs.title: Custom Functions
docs.text:
Write Java methods using the official template, package them into a JAR, and upload it to ruleuler-server. Standalone ruleuler-client instances pull the JAR to disk and load it into the classpath at startup. The server never executes user code.

Write methods from template → mvn package → Upload JAR

Do not add ruleuler-client as a dependency of your function JAR, do not manually copy JARs into lib/, and do not rebuild this repository to add functions.

docs.title: Three Steps
docs.text:
1. Copy templates/ruleuler-function/ and implement your stateless methods following the template class.
  2. Run mvn package and upload the generated JAR (via the Admin Console or the curl command in the template — both call the same endpoint).
  3. Publish the knowledge package that references the action library. Restart ruleuler-client so the new JAR is loaded into the classpath.

REA call syntax: GEOFUNCTIONS.DISTANCEKM(...) (both bean ID and method name in uppercase).

docs.title: Startup & Version Updates
docs.text:
Stage Behavior Initial Deployment Pulls JARs to disk early in startup according to ruleuler.projects / RULEULER_PROJECTS. If PropertiesLauncher has already expanded the classpath, the process re-launches itself once with the same arguments Updating & Publishing Functions at Runtime Writes the new JAR to disk. If neither push nor pull has all required JARs ready, the new package is rejected and the existing package continues running. Restarting ruleuler-client is required to load updated classes Encountering New Dependencies at Runtime Downloads synchronously, then rejects the new package until the client restarts

Hot-reload never swaps loaded Java classes in-place; loader.path and Spring auto-configuration are startup-time mechanisms.

Startup pre-pull requires configuring RULEULER_PROJECTS (both ./start.sh and docker compose default to RULEULER_PROJECTS=airport_gate_allocation_db).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Uploading custom functions distributes executable bytecode to all ruleuler-client instances serving that project. Access is controlled per project (project:function:upload / project:function:view) and recorded in audit logs.

Client pull endpoints are protected by client↔server IP whitelist authentication.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: Item Rule Execution Location Standalone ruleuler-client, never ruleuler-server Statelessness Methods must be thread-safe for concurrent execution Parameter Types String / Integer / Long / Double / BigDecimal / Boolean / Date / List / Map. Object and custom POJOs are prohibited. Date = java.util.Date Return Types void or any type from the parameter table above Method Overloading Prohibited; duplicate method names fail at compile time Gray Release Conditions Custom functions cannot be called inside gray routing condition expressions function-package Must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+, stored on disk as <function-package>.jar

docs.title: Common Pitfalls
docs.text: Pitfall Fact Replacing a JAR Requires restarting ruleuler-client to enter the classpath; package refresh only writes to disk and rejects the new package until restart Initial Startup start.sh / Docker Compose pre-pulls the sample project by default; no pre-pull occurs if RULEULER_PROJECTS is unset Changing Signatures / Deleting Methods Re-save and re-publish all rules referencing the method Rollback Historical JAR versions are retained in the database; rolling back a release points dependencies back to the previous version without re-uploading the JAR

docs.title: Template Upload
docs.text: The template pom.xml uses exec-maven-plugin + curl to call POST /api/projects/{project}/function-jars with a bearer token.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Release Management module provides an approval workflow for publishing knowledge packages so that rule changes go through automated testing and human review before going live.

Core workflow: Submit → Auto Test → Review → Publish.

docs.title: Approval Workflow
docs.text:
Submit Release Request
    │
    ├─ Has Test Case Pack ──→ TESTING (Async Auto Test) ──→ PENDING (Awaiting Review)
    │
    └─ No Test Case Pack  ──→ PENDING (Awaiting Review)
                                  │
                        ┌─────────┼─────────┐
                        ↓                   ↓
                   APPROVED            REJECTED
              (Ready to Publish)       (Rejected)
                        │
                        ↓
                 Execute Publish
                        │
                  ┌─────┼─────┐
                  ↓           ↓
              PUBLISHED   PUBLISH_FAILED
              (Live)      (Failed, Retryable)

docs.title: Status Definitions
docs.text: Status Description TESTING Automated test suite is running; transitions to PENDING upon completion PENDING Awaiting reviewer approval APPROVED Approved and ready to publish REJECTED Rejected by reviewer PUBLISHED Live in production PUBLISH_FAILED Publish failed; can be retried

docs.title: Submitting a Release
docs.text:
Required permission: pack:publish:submit

When a release request is submitted, the system automatically performs:

  1. Uniqueness Check: Only one active PENDING approval request is allowed per knowledge package at a time
  2. Automatic Versioning: Every save of a decision component creates an immutable version record (V1, V2, V3...) in ruleuler_rule_file_version
  3. Version Locking: Traverses the decision flow XML and replaces all version="LATEST" references with the exact current version number (e.g., V3)
  4. Content Snapshot: Saves the version-locked XML content of all decision resources in the project into ruleuler_publish_snapshot
  5. Content-Level Diff: Compares the current snapshot against the previous published snapshot to compute component-, row-, and field-level diffs
  6. Automated Testing: If the knowledge package has an associated test case pack, triggers an asynchronous test run

docs.title: Version Locking Mechanism
docs.text:
Decision flows reference child rule files via file + version attributes. In the editor, version="LATEST" is used by default.

Without version locking, edits made after submitting an approval request would silently slip into the built knowledge package when published.

Version locking pipeline:

Save aircraft_gate_map.dt.xml in editor
    → Automatically creates version V5 in ruleuler_rule_file_version

Submit Approval
    → Reads decision flow XML: file="dbr:/xxx/aircraft_gate_map.dt.xml" version="LATEST"
    → Queries latest version of that resource: V5
    → Rewrites reference to: file="dbr:/xxx/aircraft_gate_map.dt.xml" version="V5"
    → Saves locked XML into ruleuler_publish_snapshot

Publish
    → Builds knowledge package from the locked snapshot
    → Decision flow references version="V5"
    → DatabaseResourceProvider reads V5 from ruleuler_rule_file_version
    → Even if the file was later edited to V6, the published package strictly runs V5

docs.title: Content-Level Diff
docs.text:
Diffs are computed directly from XML content rather than version numbers across three levels of granularity:

  • Component Level: Identifies ADDED, MODIFIED, and DELETED decision components
  • Rule Row Level: For MODIFIED components, parses individual rules by resource type:
  • Decision Table (.dt.xml): Grouped by cell row attribute
  • Rule Set (.rs.xml): Matched by rule name attribute
  • REA Rule (.rea.xml): Matched by rea-item name attribute
  • Decision Flow (.rl.xml): Matched by node name attribute
  • Decision Tree (.dtree.xml): Matched by node var / var-label attribute
  • Field Level: Extracts exact condition, assignment, and cell changes (e.g., arrival_time >= : 6.8 → 6.9)

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Required permission: pack:publish:approve

Reviewers can:

  • Approve: Transitions status to APPROVED with an optional comment (≤500 characters)
  • Reject: Transitions status to REJECTED with a rejection reason

The approval detail page displays basic metadata, submitter change notes, automated test summary, and expandable component/row/field diffs.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
Required permission: pack:publish:submit

Only requests in APPROVED or PUBLISH_FAILED status can be published.

Publishing builds the knowledge package from the locked snapshot, pushes it to ruleuler-client, and records the snapshot as the new baseline for future diffs.

docs.title: Gray Release / A/B Testing
docs.text: In addition to full rollouts, RulEuler supports Gray Release (A/B Testing) to split live traffic between the baseline (BASE) and gray (GRAY) versions of a knowledge package.

docs.title: Routing Strategies
docs.text:
1. PERCENTAGE (Percentage Split):
  2. Routes a configured percentage of traffic (e.g., 10% to GRAY, 90% to BASE).
  3. CONDITION (Condition Expression):
  4. Routes requests matching an REA condition expression (e.g., FlightInfo.is_international == TRUE or user_type == "VIP") to the GRAY version.

docs.title: Gray Lifecycle
docs.text:
While a gray rule is active (ACTIVE), operators can monitor hit/success/fail counts and average latency for BASE vs. GRAY, then either:

  • Full Rollout (ROLLED_OUT): Promote the gray version to become the primary baseline version
  • Rollback (ROLLED_BACK): Deactivate the gray routing rule and revert all traffic to the baseline version

docs.title: UI Views
docs.text: View Route Description Pending Review /releases/pending Reviewer view showing PENDING requests Ready to Publish /releases/pending-publish Shows APPROVED requests My Requests /releases/my Requests submitted by the current user All Requests /releases/all All approval requests with status filtering

docs.title: Rule Set
docs.text:
A Rule Set (.rs.xml) is the foundational rule type, containing multiple if-then-else rules.

Use case: Straightforward conditional checks and variable assignments.

IF FlightInfo.passenger_count > 200 AND FlightInfo.is_international
THEN GateResult.gate_type = "Contact Gate"; GateResult.reason = "International flight priority"

Supports two editing modes:

  • Wizard Mode — Configure conditions and actions through form selectors
  • REA Expression Editor — Write rules directly in concise text syntax (see REA Expressions)

docs.title: Decision Table
docs.text:
A Decision Table (.dt.xml) organizes rules as a matrix where rows represent condition combinations and columns represent conditions and output actions.

Use case: Multi-condition combinations that benefit from side-by-side tabular comparison.

Flight Type Passenger Count Gate Type Reason International > 200 Contact Gate High-volume international flight International ≤ 200 Contact Gate International flight priority Domestic > 300 Contact Gate Ultra-high passenger volume Domestic ≤ 300 Remote Stand Standard domestic flight

docs.title: Decision Tree
docs.text:
A Decision Tree (.dtree.xml) organizes conditional branches in a tree hierarchy.

Use case: Conditions with a clear hierarchical order, evaluating broad categories before finer subdivisions.

docs.title: Decision Flow
docs.text:
A Decision Flow (.rl.xml) orchestrates multiple rule nodes using a visual flowchart.

Use case: Complex business workflows requiring multiple rule components to execute sequentially or along conditional branches.

Decision flows are the primary entry point for external API invocations via /process/{project}/{packageId}/{flowId}.

docs.title: Scorecard
docs.text:
A Scorecard (.sc) is used for scoring models where each condition contributes a weighted score toward a final aggregated total.

Use case: Credit scoring, risk assessment, and priority ranking.

docs.title: Script Decision Table
docs.text: A Script Decision Table (.dts.xml) extends decision tables with script expressions for custom calculation logic.

docs.title: Storage Modes
docs.text:
RulEuler supports two storage backends for rule files:

Mode Resource Prefix Description db dbr: Stored in the ruleuler_rule_file relational table; supports nested subfolders jcr No prefix Stored in an Apache Jackrabbit JCR repository

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
db mode is recommended:

  • All rule files and version histories are stored directly in MySQL for straightforward backup and migration
  • Supports organizing rule files into nested subfolders
  • Shares the same database as RBAC, release approvals, and automated testing

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
Warning

The storage mode is selected when creating a project and cannot be changed afterward. Do not mix db and jcr resource paths within the same project.

docs.title: Traffic Replay
docs.text: Traffic Replay validates the real-world impact of rule changes by sampling historical requests from ClickHouse, re-executing them against the current knowledge package version, and comparing the outputs field by field against the original execution results.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CH as ClickHouse Logs
    participant R as Replay Engine
    participant KP as Current Knowledge Package
    participant D as Diff Comparator

    R->>CH: Sample execution_id list
    loop Each execution
        R->>CH: Fetch input/output variable rows
        R->>R: Reconstruct input (grouped by category)
        R->>KP: Insert input → startProcess(flowId)
        KP-->>R: Execution output (modified fields only)
        R->>D: compare(original output, replay output)
        D-->>R: DiffResult (SAME / CHANGED / ADDED / REMOVED)
    end

Core pipeline:

  1. Sample historical execution_id records from ClickHouse execution_var_log
  2. Fetch all variable rows per execution_id to reconstruct the input payload and original output
  3. Execute the replay locally against the current knowledge package via KnowledgeSession
  4. Retain only fields modified relative to the input (aligned with online logging behavior)
  5. Compare original vs. replayed outputs field by field to generate a diff report

docs.title: Sampling Strategies
docs.text: Strategy Description random Random sampling for quick validation uniform Evenly spaced sampling across the selected time window all Full replay of all matching executions in the time window

docs.title: Missing Variable Handling
docs.text:
Historical logs may lack newly added variables. Three handling strategies are supported:

Strategy Description segment Fill with the variable's default or zero value and mark as INCOMPLETE null Leave missing variables as null skip Skip incomplete execution records

docs.title: Field-Level Diffs
docs.text:
Each output field is classified as:

Status Meaning SAME Original and replayed values match CHANGED Value changed between original and replay ADDED Replay produced a field not present in the original output REMOVED Original output had a field that was not produced during replay

Numeric tolerance (exact match, absolute tolerance, or relative tolerance) is supported to avoid false positives from floating-point precision.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Project Details → Traffic Replay (or Release Management → Traffic Replay)
  2. Select the knowledge package, time range, and sampling strategy
  3. Click Create to start the replay task
  4. Inspect the replay report: match rate, per-variable change statistics, latency comparison (average and P95), and per-request field diffs
  5. Export to Test Cases: Export all, mismatched-only, or matched-only replay records into an automated test case pack for future regression runs

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ClickHouse is configured and contains historical execution logs (Variable Monitoring enabled)
  • The target knowledge package is published and loadable
